key_insight: Trial-level auditory oddball ERP waveforms analyzed with deep learning distinguished schizophrenia from healthy controls better than conventional ERP summary-feature models.
clinical_relevance: This suggests waveform-level EEG biomarkers may help support future individual-level psychiatric classification, though the work is not a standalone diagnostic tool.
method: 258 patients with schizophrenia and 142 healthy controls were studied using an auditory duration oddball EEG paradigm.
Trial-level mismatch ERP waveforms were created from accepted deviant trials and residualized for demographic effects using training data only.
Five deep learning models were compared with classical machine learning models trained on 18 ERP summary features.
evidence_signal: On a fixed participant-level split, deep learning achieved test AUROC values of 0.797 to 0.857, outperforming feature-based classical models at 0.705 to 0.720.
watch_item: Performance was evaluated on a single split with a specific preprocessing pipeline, so external validation is needed before broader use.
paper_title: Deep Learning for Individual-Level Classification of Schizophrenia Versus Healthy Controls from Trial-Level Auditory Oddball ERP Waveforms
